title: Qualify the ISA-L XOR comparator
description:
Establish the exact ISA-L XOR arm that can be compared with the canonical mid-range logical operation, including its build and representation adapter contract.

## Background

ISA-L's public dispatched `xor_gen` route requires NASM; the earlier base-only build is useful context but is not SIMD evidence. The qualification must either reproduce the dispatched route on a prepared host or preserve its unavailability explicitly, while keeping `xor_gen_base` labelled as a scalar base arm.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed comparator specification pins the ISA-L revision, license, build flags, NASM version or observed absence, selected symbol, input/output semantics, and reproducible build commands.
- [hard] REQ-02: A semantic probe demonstrates matching LSB-first XOR behavior and accounts for destination setup, pointer arrays, alignment, conversion, and output costs, or records why no comparable dispatched arm is available.

## Notes

Grounding: `dev/active/2037941f-profile-and-optimize-mid-range-buffer-operations/investigation.md` and the linked Zen 3 measurement contract.

planning.outcome: ISA-L comparator semantics and dispatched-route availability fixed before protocol freezing

footprint.uncertainty: A small probe may live beside the comparator document or in its eventual receipt directory depending on the existing external-build harness.

title: Freeze the logical-buffer measurement addendum
description:

## Background

The protocol covers 8, 9, 63, 64, and 65 words, deliberately offset views, neighboring sizes, relevant cache regimes, and both isolated and whole-consumer costs. It uses a public `row_xor` route plus one coding or elimination route whose actual stride lies in the story band. The ISA-L arm follows the qualified comparator specification and remains explicitly base-only if dispatched SIMD is unavailable.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The addendum pins operations, input identities, alignments, cache regimes, seeds, warmup, sample bounds, repetitions, primary cells, estimator, confidence procedure, outlier policy, multiple-comparison family, search budget, and stopping rule before confirmation.
- [hard] REQ-02: Family-specific worthwhile-effect, equivalence-margin, complexity, and measurement-resolution rules distinguish isolated throughput from whole-consumer benefit and retain negative or unavailable cells.
- [hard] REQ-03: The addendum excludes the preserved 64-word generic dispatch-hoist no-win from the candidate search unless a materially different consumer contract is demonstrated.

## Notes

The normative measurement rules are in `dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md`.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One family addendum over already inventoried logical routes

title: Confirm the dense-parity production outcome
description:
Run holdout confirmation for the selected dense-parity outcome against the pinned current baseline, or publish the final no-change verdict.

## Background

A production change requires allocated whole-`matvec` before/after evidence on the exact declared domain plus neighboring non-regression cells. A no-adoption decision preserves the complete fusion and M4RI record and explains why the current fused AND-popcount route remains selected.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Any production change has paired or interleaved holdout samples against the pinned pre-change baseline with adjusted confidence bounds and equivalence-margin results for primary and neighboring cells.
- [hard] REQ-02: Allocated whole-`matvec` cells demonstrate the predeclared worthwhile benefit without regression outside the selected domain; otherwise the change is not accepted and contradictory evidence remains committed.
- [hard] REQ-03: The receipt pins contract, addendum, executable, configuration, inputs, runtime provenance, assembly, profiles, and exact commands by content identity.

## Notes

Run only in the benchmark window on the prepared host under the full-host wrapper.

planning.outcome: Dense-parity adoption receives holdout evidence or closes with preserved no-change

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One selected route with a frozen confirmation matrix

footprint.uncertainty: The final receipt is created under dev/bench_results/<created-issue-short-id>/ after batch creation assigns this issue an identifier.

title: Confirm the zero-copy production outcome
description:
Run holdout confirmation for an approved zero-copy production integration, or publish the final no-change verdict.

## Background

Only a qualifying and architecture-approved integration receives before/after measurement. The confirmation includes copying, offset handling, masking, dispatch, setup, and output costs in the same whole-consumer boundary used by the prototype.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Any adopted integration has paired or interleaved holdout samples against the pinned pre-change baseline with adjusted confidence bounds and equivalence-margin results.
- [hard] REQ-02: Whole-consumer benefit survives all adapter costs and semantic checks; otherwise the integration is not accepted and the contradictory evidence remains committed.
- [hard] REQ-03: The receipt pins contract, addendum, executable, configuration, inputs, runtime provenance, profiles, and exact commands by content identity, while a no-adoption path records why no after measurement is applicable.

## Notes

Run only in the benchmark window on the prepared host under the full-host wrapper.

planning.outcome: Zero-copy adoption receives holdout evidence or closes with preserved no-change

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One approved route with a frozen confirmation matrix

title: Publish the mid-range evidence synthesis
description:
Publish the final story-level evidence index and criterion interpretation without duplicating the raw receipts.

## Background

The synthesis links the frozen protocols, baseline and candidate receipts, external comparisons, adoption decisions, holdout confirmations, annotated assembly, and profiles. It preserves negative, unavailable, inconclusive, and contradictory outcomes and states which production routes remain selected.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A concise findings document maps each story criterion to content-pinned artifacts and distinguishes isolated throughput from measured consumer benefit.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every empirical claim names its sample count, confidence interval or equivalence result, producing identity, host, and toolchain; raw data remain linked rather than copied.
- [hard] REQ-03: Residual gaps have a measured limit, preserved experiment, or tracked falsifiable follow-up within the frozen search budget, and no finite search is described as an absolute optimum.
- [hard] REQ-04: The selected or retained production routes and all no-win outcomes are stated consistently with the canonical buffer boundary and external-comparison rules.

## Notes

Permanent documentation changes are required only when the final selected production behavior changes a user-facing contract.

planning.outcome: Story evidence mapped to criteria with selected routes and preserved no-wins

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One concise synthesis over already reviewed durable artifacts
